documents.title: Primary Care Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
NEW PATIENT VISIT

55 y/o woman transferring care; prior PCP retiring. Brought her bottles.

Hx:
- HTN for ~10 yrs. Amlodipine 10 + HCTZ 25. Doesn't check at home.
- T2DM dx about 8 yrs ago. Metformin 1000 bid, glargine 20 u qhs. Says sugars "have never been great"; recent outside A1c values in the low 8s per her report. Checks fingersticks a few times a week, fasting mostly.
- RA since her late 30s, seropositive. Outside rheumatologist, seen about yearly. MTX 15 mg weekly + folic acid, prednisone 5 daily for about 10 yrs. Hands are "okay most days."
- Iron deficiency anemia, on ferrous sulfate. Colonoscopy at 50 had a polyp removed; she has not been back.
- Bone density "a little thin" on a scan at the old office, put down to the steroid.

PSH: C-section at 28. Colonoscopy w/ polypectomy at 50.
FH: Mother - T2DM, HTN, stroke at 72. Father - CAD, MI at 68. Sister - seropositive RA. Maternal aunt - breast cancer (IDC) at 62.
SH: Part-time bookkeeper. Smokes ~1 ppd, 30 pack-years. Wine a glass or two a month. No drugs.
Allergies: NKDA.

ROS: negative except as above. No chest pain, dyspnea, edema, GI bleeding, melena.

Exam: Pleasant, in no distress. Vitals per flowsheet. HEENT unremarkable. Neck supple, no thyromegaly. Heart RRR, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, nontender, low transverse scar. Ext: no edema. Hands: mild MCP thickening bilaterally, no warmth or effusion. Feet: skin intact, pulses 2+, monofilament intact both feet.

A/P:
1. T2DM, not at goal by history. A1c, CMP, UACR today. Continue metformin and glargine for now; revisit once I have numbers.
2. HTN - reasonable today. Continue amlodipine/HCTZ.
3. RA on MTX/pred - per rheumatology. CBC and LFTs here every few months if she wants them local; she does.
4. IDA - CBC, iron studies. Overdue surveillance colonoscopy given prior adenoma and the anemia: GI referral.
5. Steroid osteopenia - will get the old DXA from her records; repeat when due.
6. Tobacco - 30 pk-yr, current. Talked about quitting; she isn't ready. Qualifies for annual LDCT - ordered.
7. HM: Tdap today. HCV and HIV screening today. Screening mammogram ordered (last one last fall, normal per pt).

Records release on file. RTC 3 months.

documents.title: Patient Portal Message
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Hi Janet, your labs from Tuesday are back.
- A1c is 8.3, which is above the target we talked about (under 7.5 or so for you).
- Kidney function and liver tests look fine, which matters with the methotrexate.
- Hemoglobin is mildly low and your iron stores are low, so keep taking the iron every day.
- Urine protein screen was normal. Hepatitis C and HIV screens were negative.
- Cholesterol: LDL 118.
We'll go over the sugar plan at your December visit. The GI office should call you to set up the colonoscopy.

- A1c values 2016-2019 in the 8s.
- DXA 2016: osteopenia (report included, values not legible on fax copy).
- Colonoscopy 2014: one small tubular adenoma removed; 5-year recall advised.
- Mammograms yearly through 10/2018, all BI-RADS 1.
- Immunizations: flu yearly; pneumococcal not documented; Tdap not found.
- Allergies: none recorded.

Placed in chart. Flagged to PCP: colonoscopy recall was due 2019.

documents.title: Colonoscopy Report
documents.author: gastroenterology
documents.body:
OUTSIDE GASTROENTEROLOGY - PROCEDURE REPORT
Procedure date: 02/12/2020
Indication: Surveillance; history of adenoma (2014). Iron deficiency anemia.
Allergies: NKDA.
Sedation: monitored anesthesia care.
Prep: good (BBPS 8).
Findings: Scope advanced to the cecum; appendiceal orifice and ileocecal valve photographed. Scattered diverticula in the sigmoid colon. No polyps. No mass, no blood, no angioectasia. Retroflexion in the rectum normal.
Impression: Sigmoid diverticulosis. No polyps.
Recommendation: High-fiber diet. Repeat colonoscopy in 7 years. Anemia evaluation of the upper tract at the discretion of the referring physician.

documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Video visit (pandemic). Pt at home, ID verified, consents to video.
Working from home for now, more snacking, less walking. Fasting sugars 130s-160s. Home cuff readings 130s/80s.
RA: hands stiff in the mornings about 30 minutes, not worse than usual. Rheum appointment pushed to the fall.
Colonoscopy in Feb showed diverticulosis only, no polyps; report reviewed.
Smoking about the same.

- HTN: home numbers ok.
- RA/MTX: due for CBC, CMP.
- Tobacco: discussed; not ready.
F/u in office in summer.

documents.title: Primary Care Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
DM/HTN follow-up. Masked, screened at door.
Back at the office 3 days a week. Fasting sugars 120-170. No lows. Feet ok. Some mornings with stiffer hands, nothing new.
Exam: Heart RRR. Lungs clear. Abd benign. No pedal edema. Monofilament normal bilaterally.
A/P:
- T2DM above goal. She'd rather keep working on diet before changing anything; we'll recheck A1c at her wellness visit in October.
- HTN controlled.
- Iron deficiency: Hb steady. Continue iron.
- Smoking: unchanged, cut back a few cigarettes on work days. Encouraged.
Next: Medicare wellness visit in October with flu shot and fasting labs.

documents.title: Rheumatology Follow-up Letter
documents.author: rheumatology
documents.body:
OUTSIDE RHEUMATOLOGY - CLINIC LETTER
Visit date: 09/14/2020
Dear colleague,
I saw Ms. Krause for her yearly review of seropositive rheumatoid arthritis, now of about 19 years. She reports morning stiffness of about half an hour and no recent flares. Exam: mild bony MCP enlargement bilaterally without synovitis today; no nodules. Allergies: none known.
Medications: methotrexate 15 mg weekly with folic acid 1 mg daily; prednisone 5 mg daily.
Plan: continue the current regimen. CBC and liver panel every 3 months - happy for these to be drawn at your office and copied to us. Return in 12 months.
With thanks.

documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
MEDICARE ANNUAL WELLNESS VISIT (initial)

Health risk assessment reviewed with patient. Lives in her own home; independent in all ADLs/IADLs. Drives. No falls this year. Hearing and vision adequate by self report; last eye exam over two years ago. No advance directive yet - forms given, she will think about naming her sister.
Depression screen negative. Cognition: normal recall and clock draw.

Current problems: HTN, T2DM, RA, IDA, steroid osteopenia, tobacco use.
Meds reconciled - same 8.
FH/SH unchanged; still ~1 ppd.

Exam: Vitals per flowsheet. Well appearing. Heart RRR, no murmurs. Lungs clear. Breasts deferred to imaging per pt preference. Abd soft. No edema. Feet with intact sensation and pulses.

Prevention plan:
- Flu today. Shingrix #1 today; #2 in 2-6 months (nurse visit).
- Screening mammogram and repeat LDCT ordered.
- Diabetic eye exam - referral to optometry.
- Colonoscopy 2/2020, next 2027.
- DXA: last 2016 per records; repeat in the spring.
- Tobacco: 3 min counseling; precontemplative.
- Fasting labs today.
Personalized prevention schedule printed for her.
